A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoodAngels framework and MoodSyn dataset. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original diagnostic experiments, ablations, scale-correlation analyses and synthetic-data evaluations, including Tables 3–6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds clinician evaluations, demographic analyses and sensitivity experiments in Appendices D and E.

M1.justification: The item selection, BGE-M3 retrieval, three diagnostic variants, judged debate and synthetic-data generation remain unchanged. Appendix C.4.1 newly specifies debate stages and round limits, but does not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same hospital dataset and MoodSyn for mood-disorder diagnosis. The new clinician audits and demographic analyses examine existing data and outputs; they do not establish additional clinical populations, datasets or diagnostic tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds medgemma-27b-text-it as an evaluated baseline in both the real-data and synthetic-data comparisons in Tables 3 and 4. The earlier comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 50-case clinician discrimination study, three-expert reasoning ratings, demographic subgroup evaluation, and retrieval-count, input-order and temperature experiments. Table 1 also changes the test counts from 56 mood-disorder/190 other-disorder cases to 190/56, while Section 4.1 retains the earlier counts. This establishes inconsistent reported settings, not that the dataset changed or experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained record-format and scale-selection ablations, v2 tests retrieval depth, debate-input ordering and temperature sensitivity, examines demographic performance, and adds clinician assessments of synthetic realism and generated reasoning. Figure 6 adds a worked debate example. These substantially broaden the questions investigated.

E5.justification: V1 already reports Pearson-correlation p-values. V2 additionally reports Fleiss' kappa for the clinician studies and p-values for gender and age comparisons. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty estimates for the main diagnostic benchmarks.

E6.justification: Existing performance entries in Tables 3–6 are unchanged. V2 adds MedGemma accuracies of 0.743 on real data and 0.704 on synthetic data, clinician-evaluation results, subgroup scores and sensitivity results in Tables 16 and 18–24. These substantially expand the reported outcomes rather than demonstrate a same-setting improvement of the original method.

T1.justification: The binary task definition, embedding-similarity formulation and synthetic-data mathematical descriptions are retained. V2 introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same novelty, diagnostic-performance and privacy-preserving dataset claims. The additional experiments do not redefine the principal contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its new evaluations as supporting demographic generalization, diagnostic stability and clinician-recognized reasoning quality. It also explains the initial-stage binary diagnosis rationale and qualifies retrieval depth as dataset-dependent. The existing limitations discussion is retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4.1 newly documents the debate stages and two-to-four-round limits, and Table 24 identifies the default temperature as 1. V1's explicit statement that data processing uses GPT-4o followed by manual revision is omitted. Most prompts, hardware information and resource links are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds the MedGemma report and four references concerning interpretable mental-health analysis and biomedical language models. The related-work discussion and claimed positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 extensively reorganizes the appendices into framework, agent, synthetic-data and experiment sections, consolidates repeated prompt descriptions, relocates ethics and limitations before the references, and adds a NeurIPS checklist. The main scientific narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 converts existing prompts into consolidated tables, reformats the correlation listing into two columns, pairs existing case figures, and adds a debate diagram and evaluation tables. V1's reproduced IRB document is absent from v2, which instead refers to separate supplemental materials.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful comparisons, sensitivity checks and clearer debate documentation, but important new evidence is internally inconsistent. Table 20 reports multi-Angels coherence of 1.3 although the displayed rater scores average 1.0; Table 16's counts conflict with its stated accuracies; and revised Table 1 conflicts with Section 4.1. These problems undermine the added validation, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
